item.title: Color, Composition and One Very Large Couch
item.description: English Pre-Raphaelite Albert Joseph Moore, A.R.W.S. (1841-1893) painted “Apples” (above) in 1875. Moore was a painter of the “art for art’s sake” variety; he sought classical beauty first and foremost, avoiding strong statement or deeper meaning. His paintings, like those of his good friend James McNeill Whistler, are professedly experiments with formal elements such as color [...]
